glosses: Évoluer dans un sens favorable.

examples.text: Le temps s’arrange.

glosses: Prendre ses dispositions, se débrouiller pour arriver à un résultat.

examples.text: Je veux passer avant tes girls, expliquait-il au régisseur. Arrange-toi pour ne pas me faire poireauter. Avec elles, on n’en finit plus.
Quels que soient les services que je pourrai vous rendre, je m’arrangerai pour que nous soyons entièrement quittes.

glosses: S’accommoder, prendre son parti de quelque chose.

examples.text: C’est petit mais on s’en arrangera.

– Quant aux journalistes…
– Vous vous en arrangerez, n’est-ce pas ?
Une amitié pouvait s’arranger de ces divergences ; elles rendaient redoutable la perspective d’une vie commune.
Il ne s'agit pas d'être indifférent en disant : « C'est son problème, qu'il ou elle s'en arrange. »

glosses: Régler par voie de conciliation, se mettre d’accord.

examples.text: Ils n’ont pas tardé à s’arranger entre eux.
Vous vous arrangerez avec l'administrateur.

glosses: Ordonner avec goût sa toilette, sa coiffure, etc.

examples.text: Et elle s’applique et se multiplie ; elle met beaucoup de temps à s’arranger, mais ce sont des heures importantes et non perdues.
Leurs compagnes ouvraient leurs sacs, y prenaient un miroir et s’arrangeaient coquettement les cheveux.

glosses: S’améliorer, devenir plus séduisant.

examples.text: Ils ne se sont pas arrangés avec l’âge !

glosses: To calculate.

examples.text: Can you work out 250 × 12 in your head for me?
Can you work out how to get to the university by car?
You don't have to be Einstein to work out that this level of government subsidy is unsustainable.

glosses: To make sense of.

examples.text: I can't work these instructions out.

glosses: To decide.

examples.text: I can't work out if I like him or not.

glosses: To bring about or cause to happen by work or effort.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: hash out, hammer out
I think we can work out a compromise.
"Ah! if man would but see that hope is from within and not from without - that he himself must work out his own salvation!"

glosses: To resolve; to find a solution for.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: straighten out, sort out
They managed to work out their differences.
Trump hinted that Britain might be spared tariffs, saying: “I think that one can be worked out”.

glosses: To develop or devise in detail; to elaborate.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: plan out, lay out
to work out a plan

glosses: To smooth or perfect.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: iron out, smooth out
This is a beta version; we're still working out the kinks.

glosses: To conclude with the correct solution.

examples.text: Near-synonym: add up
These figures just don't work out.

glosses: To succeed; to result in a satisfactory situation.

examples.text: Near-synonym: pan out
Are you still seeing John? – No, it didn't work out.
As everyone knows, almost all booked passenger and freight trains are diagrammed into rosters for engines and men, and in an operating Utopia everything would work out daily according to plan.

glosses: To exercise, especially by lifting weights.

examples.text: John won't be here for a while because he's working out.
Wow, you're looking good! Do you work out?

glosses: To strengthen a part of one’s body by exercise.

examples.text: To work out your core
Hot, worked-out body and a creative mind possessed by this hunky, handsome, married guy.

glosses: To earn a wage working away from one's farm.

examples.text: The two Russians made good farmhands, and in summer they worked out together.
[…] with them good wages, maybe a fella can get hisself a little piece a land an’ work out for extra cash.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see work, out.

examples.text: Using some tweezers, he worked the bee sting out of his hand.
He works out of a small office shared with three others.

glosses: To remove all the mineral that can be profitably exploited.

examples.text: The gravel pit had been worked out.
A worked-out chalk pit or quarry

glosses: To separate and recover (valuable minerals) by swirling dirt or crushed rock in a pan of water, in the manner of a traditional prospector seeking gold.

examples.text: On the Saturday holidays in summer-time we used to borrow skiffs whose owners were not present and go down the river three miles to the cave hollow (Missourian for "valley"), and there we staked out claims and pretended to dig gold, panning out half a dollar a day at first.

His father came out in '49 with the gold rush crowd, panned out a good pile, and then, liking the life—San Francisco was a gay little burg those days—opened one of the crack gambling houses down on the Old Plaza.

glosses: To proceed according to plan; to result or end up with an acceptable outcome or in an acceptable form.

examples.text: My hopes for a white Christmas didn't pan out this year.
We'll see what pans out from the arbitration process.
Many a pretty girl I have seen in my time, who didn't pan out according to specifications when I finally met her.
That was just a theory! There's a lot of theories that didn't pan out: lone gunman, communism, geometry…
The China market is finally panning out, thanks to the voracious consumerism of the middle class.
"It is anybody's guess how this is going to pan out. The Government will have even more control of the railway than before, with no incentive to innovate. [...]"
“It’s not a goodbye because you never know how things pan out in the future, but it’s a thank you and I’ll see you soon,” Kane posted on his social media accounts.
